A frame that returns no attributes is refused, naming the look it owes (review: rich-animation-42lg.0wr)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

An effect moves only the attributes a look names (review: rich-animation-42lg.0wr)

withAttributes reads ATTRIBUTE_NAMES off its argument; Effected picks the
look's attributes through cellAttributes, the one place reverse is left out,
and skips the extra Style when a run's attributes are the segment's own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

An effect moves a cell's attributes, not only its colours (rich-animation-42lg.0wr)

An effect's frame maps a cell's look — its colours and its text attributes,
all but reverse — rather than its colours alone, so confined, onBeat,
Animation.all and nesting take an attribute effect with no second copy.
Effected cuts a run where the attributes change too, and a cell whose look
comes back as drawn is still written byte for byte as it was.

blink(spec) sets an attribute on the second hold of a two-hold beat; the
catalogue's new attributes section makes a blink (conceal) and a bold pulse
from it. Style gains attributes / withAttributes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

A glyph effect types, scrambles and rains on what an element draws (rich-animation-42lg.je5) (#483)

* A glyph effect types, scrambles and rains on what an element draws (rich-animation-42lg.je5)

GlyphEffected is Effected's glyph half: a GlyphEffect is handed every cell
an element draws (DrawnGlyphs: the cells, blanks included, and whether the
output is ASCII-only) and gives an Animation of a per-cell map to the text
each cell shows. One enforcer holds that text to the cell's width with no
line break or control character; an unchanged segment is yielded as it was.
It writes at every depth, no colour included, and nests with Effected.

The catalogue: typewriter and scramble (transitions through the one
transition() helper, now generic), caseWave, and particles with rain and
stars as two specs of it, each with an ASCII set drawn under asciiOnly.

Effected's grapheme walk and seed are now walkGlyphs and cellSeed, shared.

beat: a boundary is walked until at() places it in its hold and its pass.
With one hold the old predicate was always true, so beat([0.06]).nextChange(3.3)
answered 3.3 itself while placing 3.3 in the previous pass.

* Glyph effects: a cell may not join its neighbour, text is typed and not margins, whole-row drift, z checked and read by the wave (rich-animation-42lg.je5 review)

Line widths are checked after a frame, so a trailing joiner or leading combining mark that fuses across cells throws. Typewriter and scramble pace over each row's text, not the padding round it. One isBlank for scramble and particles; a wide blank takes a particle and a space. particles' drift is a whole number of rows. Every catalogue effect, colour and glyph, refuses a z that is not finite (requireZ). caseWave takes z and starts its pass there. stepped builds its beat once. The demo replays transitions on a Timeline from each run's start, so the frame's nextChange is on the Live's clock.

* A blank cell has width: a byte-order mark takes no particle (rich-animation-42lg.je5 review)

* Glyph effects: a changed cell stands apart from its neighbours, one ink test for both wrappers, zero-width cells are no text, eases settle (rich-animation-42lg.je5 review)

standsApart replaces keepsLines: only changed texts are asked, by grapheme count beside their neighbours, so a child splitting a cluster across segments draws as it did and a leading combining mark is caught. inked() in effect.ts is the one blank test for Effected and the glyph effects. typewriter/scramble settle the handed ease so the last cell lands. caseWave's band covers a wide glyph by any column. SCRAMBLE_GLYPHS spreads an ASCII string, so the module does nothing on import. stars wake once a life: step 1.5, life 1, the same frames.
